title: What a backflow test checks—and what happens next
description: Understand the field test, the difference between pass and filing, how tester eligibility works, and why the utility controls the final requirement.
prompt: What are you trying to confirm?
answer: A field test measures whether the testable assembly's checks, relief function, or air-inlet behavior meets the applicable procedure. A passing result may still need to be submitted and accepted.
urgency: Do not use a national page to assume that your property is due. Confirm the utility, device record, and notice.
diagramAlt: Backflow tester gauge connected to test cocks with pass, fail, and submit outcomes
identifiers: Due status: notice, device record, anniversary, or utility schedule.
Tester gate: certification alone may not equal utility approval.
Closeout: the utility may require a portal, form, fee, or tester submission.

choices.label: I received a notice
choices.detail: Find the named city or utility before booking.

choices.label: I need an accepted tester
choices.detail: Separate official lists from general local providers.

choices.label: The device failed
choices.detail: Use the repair, retest, and accepted-submission workflow.

choices.label: The test passed but filing is unclear
choices.detail: Find where the report must be submitted.

steps.title: Confirm the assembly and due status
steps.body: Match the service address, device ID, utility, and due date.

steps.title: Use an eligible tester
steps.body: Check both professional certification and any utility registration, list, or portal requirement.

steps.title: Run the field procedure
steps.body: The tester records device-specific readings and a pass or fail result.

steps.title: Close the record
steps.body: Confirm the accepted report, required fee, and any repair/retest follow-up.

safeChecks: Keep the notice and prior report.
Ask whether the quote includes filing fees and retest.
stopConditions: A provider cannot show the required credential
The notice utility and property utility do not match
A failed device is being treated as complete after repair only
The report route is an unofficial look-alike site
notThisDevice: An inspection is not always the same as a formal testable-assembly procedure.
A tester directory is not automatically an approved list.
Passing in the field is not always the same as accepted by the utility.
evidenceNote: The governing utility defines who must test, when, which tester is accepted, and how the report is filed.
